Lessons.Title: Wax Prints
ExplanationParagraphs: First Edition 2021 Grade 3 Unit 7 Lesson 14 original teacher lesson, preparation, four-page pupil PDF and separate The Bundle four-card blackline source were inspected on the authorized computer, including both textile photographs. This first-party authored companion connects quadrilateral recognition and repeated patterns with area and perimeter, while the original publisher images and gated assessment remain source-linked only.

The original warm-up Notice and Wonder: Textiles uses a photo of a woman selling brightly patterned wax print cloth to elicit observations about geometric designs. Students notice repeated colored shapes and discuss real fabric use. It has no unique scalar answer; teacher reviews student ideas and appropriate cultural description, without assuming a particular identity or fabric provenance from the photo.

Source Activity 14.1 asks students to DESIGN A WAX PRINT PATTERN on supplied square dot paper. The pattern must contain a rhombus, rectangle or square, AND a different quadrilateral which is NOT a rhombus, rectangle or square; EACH selected shape repeats at least FIVE times. The student must color the design so the shapes and repeated structure remain identifiable. A mere typed word or count cannot establish compliance with the source geometry; teacher checks actual colored drawing.

Source Activity 14.2 uses MLR4 Information Gap with exactly TWO distinct original paired card sets from the one-page blackline The Bundle. The first prompt asks about fabric area remaining for a shirt after pieces for a head wrap and a lapa are removed from one rectangle. The second asks how much decorative ribbon is needed along an original lapa rectangle's border PLUS the bottom hem of the shirt. The student's original four-page PDF shows only the question-exchange procedure, not the underlying numerical data.

The source original Data Card 1 and Data Card 2 must be handed by the teacher to different partners than the problem cards, and students must ask for the measurements they need, justify each request, solve independently and then exchange roles for the next card set. To preserve the mathematics and privacy of the original card interaction, the hidden source card measurements and solutions are recorded only in the internal authoring evidence ledger, NOT in the first-party pupil explanation, practice prompt, or source-facing view.

The two original card sets require attention to the distinction between cloth AREA in square feet and ribbon PERIMETER in linear feet, with a further linear length added for the shirt hem. They are not interchangeable units. Students should build area calculations from relevant measured rectangles, subtract fabric-used areas from the original bundle, and separately sum ribbon lengths along the actual target edges.

Source 3.G.A.1 and 3.MD.D.8 teaching schedule: warm-up 10 minutes, Create a Wax Print Pattern 20, Info Gap The Bundle 20, synthesis 5, restricted original Cool-down Quadrilaterals in a Pattern 5. The required materials are colored pencils/crayons/markers and standard square dot paper, plus two source problem/data card sets kept separate. Teacher uses MLR8 prompts while sharing designs and observes student verbal reasoning.

The section synthesis asks how area measures the amount of fabric available to cover, while perimeter measures the ribbon or lace needed around edges. An independent illustrative 5-foot by 3-foot rectangle has area 15 square feet and a border perimeter 16 feet; these invented illustrative values are NOT the answers or measurements of the original The Bundle cards. The gated publisher Cool-down is not accessed or reproduced, and tests/CI/Stage D/academic approval remain unexecuted.

KeyConcepts.Title: Source mathematics
KeyConcepts.Definition: Apply the mathematical quantities required by the original activity.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Preserve the source units, diagrams and teacher review boundary.
KeyConcepts.Example: A rectangle may have 15 square feet of fabric area and 16 feet of perimeter.

KeyConcepts.Title: Pattern repetition and source quadrilateral constraints
KeyConcepts.Definition: The first-party design must include a rhombus, rectangle or square and a distinct quadrilateral that is none of those.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Repeat each selected qualifying shape at least five times, with teacher-verified drawing and color.
KeyConcepts.Example: A repeated square may be paired with a repeated nonrectangular, nonrhombic trapezoid; a teacher must verify all shapes.

KeyConcepts.Title: Area, perimeter, and concealed information-gap cards
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fabric area uses square feet; trim around a border plus a shirt hem uses linear feet.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Students ask partners for the hidden original measurements; do not place publisher card data into pupil-facing prompts or copy original art.
KeyConcepts.Example: Independent 5-by-3-foot fabric has 15 sq ft area and 16 ft perimeter; hidden publisher quantities remain separate.

WorkedExamples.Title: Mathematical example
WorkedExamples.Question: An independent 5 ft by 3 ft rectangular swatch: find area and border length.
WorkedExamples.Method: Area product and perimeter double-sum are distinct.
Steps: Keep area in square feet and edge length in linear feet; these dimensions are independent examples rather than the original hidden card numbers.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 15 square feet of area, 16 feet of edging
WorkedExamples.Check: This example does not certify original open visuals or discussions.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent fabric area example (not a publisher card answer)
WorkedExamples.Question: An illustrative rectangular fabric piece measures 6 by 4 feet; how much area does it cover?
Steps: Identify width 4 feet and length 6 feet.
Report 24 square feet of fabric, not feet of border.
WorkedExamples.Check: The original MLR4 hidden source measurements remain separate and unavailable to pupils in this first-party example.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent border plus hem example
WorkedExamples.Question: A fictional 5-by-3-foot lapa needs ribbon around its border plus 2 feet of separate hem. What total length is used?
Steps: Add the hypothetical shirt hem 2 feet.
Use 16+2=18 linear feet of ribbon; do not include the fabric's 15 square feet of area.
WorkedExamples.Check: These independent numbers are not the original two-source-card measurements; teachers review card exchanges.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Grade an original open task from a single number.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original source requires modelling, visuals or explanation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check the original materials and seek teacher review.

SummaryPoints: Source photo-based Notice and Wonder is teacher-reviewed, with no forced numerical key.
Original wax-print pattern requires two different quadrilateral categories; each repeated at least five times, colored visibly.
Source separate The Bundle information-gap card pairs may not be exposed together; the original numerical answers exist only in evidence.
Area uses square feet, ribbon perimeter plus hem uses linear feet.
Original gated publisher Cool-down and Grade 3 Stage D/CI/academic signoff are not claimed.
